subject: Dedicated capacity tempo & autoscale terms — CatalyTech
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@catalytech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity tempo & autoscale terms — CatalyTech

Hi Alex,

Great talking earlier — thanks for the context on CatalyTech's production rollout. Per our call, I wanted to capture a pragmatic Dedicated plan that balances predictable baseline capacity with short, high-percentile bursts from your nightly processing jobs and weekly forecasting runs.

Key proposal (high level):
- Reserved baseline: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for steady inference traffic (pinned region: us-west-2).
- Shoulder lanes: 4x GPUs reserved for predictable daily peak windows (22:00–02:00 UTC) with pre-warming enabled.
- Ephemeral burst pool: up to +12 GPUs available on demand via autoscale policy tied to queue depth and token-rate thresholds; burst billing uses transient uplift credits (see attached capacity_model_v2.xlsx).
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up (sub-30s) on sustained queue > 1200 requests/min; conservative scale-down with 10m cooldown to avoid oscillation.
- Fallbacks: if ephemeral pool unavailable, requests will route to the next-compatible model (quantized v2) with a 95th-percentile latency guardrail.

Open items for CatalyTech input:
1) Peak duration validation — you mentioned weekly forecasting runs that last ~3–5 hours and nightly model retrains that spike for ~20–30 mins. Can you confirm typical CPU preprocessing concurrency during those windows?
2) Procurement: any constraints on committed GPU hours vs. pay-as-you-go bursting?
3) SLA uplift: do you need a 99.9% ingestion-to-first-token SLA during bursts, or is 99.5% acceptable for burst windows?

I've attached a simple capacity model to illustrate cost/tokens tradeoffs. Monica from Sales Ops is cc'd and will draft a tempo addendum once we align. Next step: if this high-level looks good, I can loop in Karthik (inference) to finalize the autoscale knobs and then get legal/procurement aligned.

Thanks,

--
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@catalytech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@catalytech.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity tempo & autoscale terms — CatalyTech

Aditya — thanks for the writeup. This maps well to our internal thinking. Quick answers below:

1) Peak durations: forecasting runs are usually 2–4 hours (peak CPU prep across ~2000 concurrent jobs), nightly inference spike is shorter — 15–40 minutes but can be high QPS (~1.5–2k reqs/min).
2) Procurement: we prefer a blended approach — commit to a baseline for pricing stability but need the option to burst without long-term hourly commitments. Would prefer credits (prepaid burst pool) over pure on-demand.
3) SLA: for customer-facing inference during spikes we need 99.8% ingestion-to-first-token. Back-office batch jobs can accept lower SLOs.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you propose a credits cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and how unused credits roll?
- Is there a guardrail for cost when the burst pool scales unexpectedly (e.g., safelimit triggers or spend caps)?

Cc'ing procurement to start the typical redline/terms discussion. Pasting Procurement: can you share the CatalyTech purchase process and PO timing?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
VP of ML Platforms, CatalyTech
alex.rivera@catalytech.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity tempo & autoscale terms — CatalyTech

Looping in some technical detail — copying Alex's notes inline for clarity.

On Fri, May 3, 2029 at 10:05 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@catalytech.com> wrote:
> 1) Peak durations: forecasting runs are usually 2–4 hours ... nightly inference spike is shorter — 15–40 minutes ...
> 2) Procurement: we prefer a blended approach ... credits (prepaid burst pool) over pure on-demand.
> 3) SLA: for customer-facing inference during spikes we need 99.8% ingestion-to-first-token.

Notes & recommended settings (technical):
- Baseline sizing: 8x A100-equivalent is sensible if your 95th-percentile request size is ~1.2k tokens and steady concurrency ~450. I'll model an additional +20% headroom for growth.
- Shoulder lanes: isolate two ~2-GPU lanes (total 4 GPUs) scheduled by cron window; pre-warm flow to populate KV cache 10 minutes before window start.
- Ephemeral burst: set max_burst=12 GPUs; scale-up policy: scale_by = min(available_pool, ceil(pending_work / 120)); scale_up_evaluation = 20s sustained threshold; scale_down_cooldown = 600s; min_stable_nodes = 2.
- Cost guardrails: recommend spend_cap = monthly_credit + 25% buffer with automatic throttling to quantized model family if the spend cap is hit. Also recommend auto-notify at 70% and 90% of credit consumption.
- Quantization/path fallbacks: we should onboard a 4-bit quantized variant for burst fallbacks; latency penalty ~8–12% but cost savings ~40%.

I attached a short draft autoscale policy for legal/ops to review (autoscale_policy_draft.pdf). Once we sign tempo addendum, we'll implement guardrails in the Dedicated control plane and add the spend_cap as an enforceable policy with webhook alerts to CatalyTech.

Technical next steps:
- Finalize exact values for pending_work threshold (Alex to confirm typical queue depth during spikes).
- Agree on monthly credit amount and rollover rule (Monica to own PO cadence and credit terms).
- If signals align, I'll provision a pre-production Dedicated slice to run your forecasting job this week for soak testing.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — aligning next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Decisions & action items:
- CatalyTech confirms peak characteristics (Alex) — Alex: please reply with a 24-hour sample of queue depth and a single representative forecasting job ID.
- Procurement cadence (Monica): propose monthly prepaid credits with 3-month rollover; initial suggested credit pool = 2500 GPU-hours/month for bursts. Monica to confirm pricing tiers and the PO timeline.
- Autoscale knobs (Karthik): implement the recommended scale_up/scale_down values; enable pre-warm for shoulder lanes; provision preprod slice for a soak test (target: 48h soak before baseline cutover).
- Cost guardrails: spend_cap enforced at control plane with automatic fallback to quantized model and notify cadence as described.
- Legal/terms: Monica will attach SOW addendum (sow-tempo-addendum.docx) and send to Alex/Procurement for redlines.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up with all stakeholders next Tue to sign off on the numbers and timeline. Tentative docu-sign link (shared below) will be live once Monica attaches the SOW.

Thanks — will keep it tight.
